_comment: How a block crops the media it was given: which part survives the crop
(focalPoint) and whether the frame is filled or fitted (objectFit).
TWO-TIER FOCAL MODEL — deliberate, not drift. This fragment's `focalPoint`
is the ENUM tier: nine named positions for a block that renders ONE piece of
media into a frame the author does not otherwise control. The numeric tier
(normalized x/y, `admin/components/blocks/composition/FocalPointPicker.vue`;
0-100 `focalX`/`focalY` on ScatterCollage items) is PER-ITEM collage geometry,
where the author is already placing the item by hand and a nine-way enum
would be a downgrade. `resolveFocalPoint()` in
`shared/features/cms/media/artDirection.ts` is the bridge: it turns an enum
token into the same {x,y} percentages the numeric tier stores, so both tiers
end up as one object-position expression.
WHY NO `aspectRatio` HERE (M1 scope decision). Ten schemas declare
`aspectRatio` today in two incompatible vocabularies: colon strings
(`16:9`, `4:3` — ImageBanner, ImageHotspots, FilterableGallery, ImageSequence,
SpotlightReveal, MapEmbed, CanvasShape, BeforeAfterReveal, ScatterCollage) and
keywords (`square`, `portrait`, `classic`, `landscape`, `wide` — CanvasImage).
Fragment ownership is theme-global — the fragment-vocabulary lint fires on
every local redeclaration whether or not the schema declared the fragment — so
owning the id forces all ten to adopt at once, and the id keeps its type and
its name while only its OPTION VALUES change. `diffSchemas()` compares field
id and field type only, so an option-value re-spelling is invisible to
auto-migration: no rename, no backup row, and every stored `wide` / `16:9`
silently falls out of vocabulary and renders as the block's fallback. Block
settings also have no `migratedFrom` read path (that exists for TEMPLATE
settings only, in `normalizeStoredTemplateSettings`), so the escape hatch used
elsewhere does not apply here. Converging the id therefore needs a value
migration over every version row — the
`2026_08_19_000003_rename_block_settings_in_all_versions` template — which is
server work and out of M1's scope.
Until then the convention is unified IN CODE, not in the schema:
`resolveAspectRatio()` accepts all three spellings and returns one CSS
`aspect-ratio` value, so adopters already share a single implementation.
WHY NO `overlayColor` / `overlayOpacity` HERE. `overlayOpacity` is declared by
four blocks across two FIELD types — `range` on HeroBlock, `number` on
ChapterDivider, LayeredComposition and ScatterCollage. A fragment owns `type`,
so owning the id forces a type change on one side or the other, and a type
change is the one diff `applyAutoMigration` resolves destructively (remove the
old value, add the new field's default). `overlayColor` has exactly one
declaring block, and the D.5b freeze forbids widening freeform per-block color
surface, so there is nothing to consolidate yet either.

settings.note: Whether the image fills the frame (cropping the overflow) or is fitted whole inside it.
Which part of the image stays in view when it is cropped to the frame.
